extracted.intended_audience: DOT rulemaking staff evaluating public comments; stakeholders and regulated parties preparing comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and preparing public comments on DOT notices of proposed rulemaking, including what makes comments effective or less impactful and how DOT processes submissions after the comment period. Intended primarily as an internal handbook for DOT rulemaking staff but also useful to stakeholders submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide empirical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide empirical evidence to support the commenter's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data, studies, analyses, or other empirical support rather than assertions; empirical support strengthens the comment's influence on agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address material errors of fact or law
rubrics_metrics.description: Address material errors of fact or law in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain factual inaccuracies or legal errors in the NPRM with citations and supporting documentation so DOT can reconsider analysis or conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise new evidence not considered by the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise new evidence the agency hasn't considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present previously unavailable data, studies, or factual information that materially bear on the rulemaking; clearly explain how the new evidence changes the agency's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite practicality and compliance issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite practicality issues in complying with the new rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain real-world compliance burdens, feasibility problems, implementation timelines, costs to regulated entities, or other practical obstacles with concrete examples or quantified impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific provisions with section citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference specific provisions with section citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct commenters to the exact NPRM sections or proposed regulatory text (section or paragraph citations) they are addressing; specific citations help staff locate and evaluate the comment's point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsupported statements of opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of opinion without supporting evidence have less impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that state preferences or opinions without factual or analytical support are unlikely to change the agency's technical or legal conclusions; bolster opinions with evidence or reasoned argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic expressions of support or opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic expressions of support or opposition are low-impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple 'I support' or 'I oppose' submissions without explanation or supporting reasons do not materially inform the agency and are less influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay on-topic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments address the issues raised in the NPRM; irrelevant material may be disregarded or assigned to other dockets and will not assist rulemaking decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission matters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within the comment period; late filings may receive reduced consideration or be excluded unless good cause is shown or the agency reopens the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the regulatory analysis (RIA, RFA, EIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with the regulatory analysis (RIA, RFA, EIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique assumptions, methods, or conclusions in the Regulatory Impact Analysis, Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis, or Environmental Impact Statement with alternative data or analyses where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantified impact estimates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer numeric estimates of costs, benefits, safety impacts, emissions, or other measurable effects; specify methodology and data sources for the estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternative regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose specific changes to the proposed regulatory language (redlines or replacement text) and explain how the alternatives address concerns or improve implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical engagement with domain-specific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical engagement with safety data, emissions data, infrastructure standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide technical analyses, references to standards, datasets, or domain-specific expertise relevant to DOT modal issues (safety, emissions, infrastructure), and explain implications for the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize competing objectives or costs and benefits; comments that weigh trade-offs and justify priorities demonstrate a reasoned approach the agency can consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow DOT submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments accepted electronically through Regulations.gov or by mail to the U.S. DOT Dockets; modal administrations have docket processes but use the unified DOT Dockets system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via Regulations.gov or mail to the Docket Clerk using the correct docket ID and modal-administration procedures to ensure the comment is properly filed and available for staff review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments demonstrating material errors may prompt reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments demonstrate material errors, the agency may reconsider the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive, documented demonstrations of material factual or legal errors can lead DOT to revise analysis, extend the comment period, re-propose a rule, or otherwise change course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect substantive-response in the final rule preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT issues the final rule with responses to substantive comments in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive comments on legal, factual, or policy matters will typically receive a reasoned response in the final rule's preamble; framing comments to raise substantive issues increases likelihood of a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: New issues may trigger additional procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments raise new issues (logical outgrowth problems), the agency may extend the comment period or re-propose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raising significant new issues that were not in the NPRM can lead the agency to reopen the record or issue a supplemental proposal; commenters should clearly identify why the issue is new and material.
